options.content:
Pick **Cluster A** and **Cluster B**. Every tile in the row below is B measured against A, each over its own whole window (a range the length of the cluster's run, evaluated at its end), so the two may have run on different days.

**What the colours mean.** Green means B is better than A, red means worse. The direction is set per metric: for latency, GC pause and errors, lower is better; for throughput, higher is better. Read the sign, not just the colour.

**Percent or absolute.** The latency, throughput, GC and allocation tiles are percent changes, empty when A is 0. The error tile is an **absolute** difference in errors per second per node, because a healthy A is zero and a percentage of zero is undefined.

**A blank tile** means one side had no data: either A was zero, or A and B are not both set.

**Comparing a cluster with itself** reads 0% everywhere. That is the expected result, and a useful check that the section is wired up.

To compare more than two clusters, open **Experiment: Cassandra**.

panels.description: Change in read latency at ${percentile}, B against A. Negative is better: B answers reads faster. The percentile is a pre-aggregated gauge from each node's EstimatedHistogram, averaged over each cluster's nodes and over its own window. Empty when A is 0.

targets.expr: 100 * ((avg(avg_over_time(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_b", cassandra_operation="read"}[${b_len}s] @ ${b_end}))) - (avg(avg_over_time(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_a", cassandra_operation="read"}[${a_len}s] @ ${a_end})))) / ((avg(avg_over_time(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_a", cassandra_operation="read"}[${a_len}s] @ ${a_end}))) != 0)

panels.title: Read ${percentile}

panels.description: Change in write latency at ${percentile}, B against A. Negative is better: B acknowledges writes faster. Empty when A is 0.

targets.expr: 100 * ((avg(avg_over_time(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_b", cassandra_operation="write"}[${b_len}s] @ ${b_end}))) - (avg(avg_over_time(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_a", cassandra_operation="write"}[${a_len}s] @ ${a_end})))) / ((avg(avg_over_time(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_a", cassandra_operation="write"}[${a_len}s] @ ${a_end}))) != 0)

panels.title: Write ${percentile}

panels.description: Change in coordinator requests per second per node, B against A. Positive is better: B serves more work. Averaged per node so clusters of different sizes stay comparable. Empty when A is 0.

targets.expr: 100 * ((avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_b"}[${b_len}s] @ ${b_end})))) - (avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_a"}[${a_len}s] @ ${a_end}))))) / ((avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_a"}[${a_len}s] @ ${a_end})))) != 0)

panels.title: Throughput

panels.description: Change in the share of wall clock time spent in stop-the-world GC pauses, B against A. Negative is better. Concurrent cycles are excluded with jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"; leaving them in counts a concurrent collector's background work as pause time and makes it look worse than a stop-the-world collector, which is backwards. Empty when A is 0.

targets.expr: 100 * ((avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_b", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"}[${b_len}s] @ ${b_end})))) - (avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_a", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"}[${a_len}s] @ ${a_end}))))) / ((avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_a", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"}[${a_len}s] @ ${a_end})))) != 0)

panels.title: GC pause overhead

panels.description: Change in bytes allocated per second per node, B against A. Negative is better only at equal throughput: allocating less for the same work means less garbage to collect. Always read it beside the Throughput tile, because a cluster doing more work allocates more. jvm_memory_allocation_bytes is a histogram, so this is the _sum series, never a _total. Needs Java 17 or newer: the OpenTelemetry agent derives allocation from JFR and emits no jvm_memory_allocation on Java 11, the default for Cassandra 4.x and 5.0 (run `cassandra use <version> --java 17`). Empty when A is 0.

targets.expr: 100 * ((avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_memory_allocation_bytes_sum{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_b"}[${b_len}s] @ ${b_end})))) - (avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_memory_allocation_bytes_sum{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_a"}[${a_len}s] @ ${a_end}))))) / ((avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_memory_allocation_bytes_sum{job="cassandra", cluster="$cluster_a"}[${a_len}s] @ ${a_end})))) != 0)

panels.title: Allocation rate

panels.description: Errors per second per node on B minus A, each over its own window. Negative is better. This one is an absolute difference, not a percentage: a healthy cluster has zero errors, and a percentage change from zero is undefined and would blank the tile.
panels.title: Error rate (absolute)

list.definition: query_result(sort_desc(max by (cluster) (max_over_time(timestamp(count by (cluster) (up{edl_tenant=~"$exp_tenant", experiment=~"$exp_name"}) or count by (cluster) (up{experiment="", cluster=~"$exp_name"}))[$lookback:${resolution}s]))))
list.description: Cluster B: a cluster of the selected experiment with up samples within Lookback, newest first. The installer selects the current cluster; with none it opens on the newest. Every difference is B measured against A.
list.label: Cluster B
list.name: cluster_b
list.query: query_result(sort_desc(max by (cluster) (max_over_time(timestamp(count by (cluster) (up{edl_tenant=~"$exp_tenant", experiment=~"$exp_name"}) or count by (cluster) (up{experiment="", cluster=~"$exp_name"}))[$lookback:${resolution}s]))))

list.definition: query_result(max by (exp_key) (label_join(last_over_time(up{cluster="$cluster_a", experiment!=""}[$lookback]), "exp_key", "/", "edl_tenant", "experiment")) or on() max by (exp_key) (label_join(label_replace(label_replace(last_over_time(up{cluster="$cluster_a", experiment=""}[$lookback]), "t", "$1", "__tenant_id__", "(.+)"), "t", "${home_tenant}", "t", ""), "exp_key", "/", "t", "cluster")))
